The numbers, and what they mean for you

Tap any line for the longer version.

  • 2,293 mmDig depthDigs to 2.3 m. Deep enough for septic, stormwater and dam work.

    From the ground to the teeth with the arm fully reached down and the tracks flat. Real-world depth is usually 10 to 15 per cent less because you are digging from a bench, not a flat pad. Most house drainage sits between 600 mm and 1.5 m down.

  • 1,300 mm to 1,500 mmWidth, tracks in1.3 m with the tracks in. Won't fit a side gate. Fine for driveways, farm gates and open sites.

    The narrowest the machine gets, with the tracks pulled in for transport. Measure your access at its tightest point and allow 50 mm of clearance either side. On site you push the tracks out again for stability.

  • 2,371 kgOperating weightAbout 2.4 tonne with a driver on board. This plus a plant trailer is at the limit of a dual-cab ute.

    The machine ready to work: full of fuel, with a bucket on and a driver in the seat. This is the number to use when you are checking what a trailer, a truck or a driveway can take.

  • 2,290 kgTransport weightWhat you are actually towing, without a driver. Add the trailer weight and check it against your tow rating carefully. A 3.5 tonne rating is the minimum.

    The machine on the trailer with no driver. Add the trailer's own weight (usually 500 to 800 kg for a plant trailer) and compare the total with your vehicle's braked towing capacity. Every dual-cab ute is different, so check the compliance plate.

  • 4,143 mmReachReaches over 4 m from the centre of the machine. The longest reach in the range.

    From the centre of the machine to the teeth with the arm stretched out at ground level. More reach means fewer moves along a trench and the ability to dig where you cannot drive.

  • 2,497 mmDump heightLifts the bucket to 2.5 m. High enough to load a tipper truck.

    How high the bucket lip gets with the arm raised. To load a tandem trailer you need about 1.5 m. A ute tray needs about 1.2 m. A small tipper needs 2.2 m or more.

  • 2,450 mmHeightClears a standard garage door, just. The cab is the tallest point.

    From the ground to the top of the canopy or cab. Compare with garage doors, carports and low branches on the way in. A standard single garage door opening is about 2.1 m high.

  • 3,949 mmLengthAbout the length of a small sedan with the bucket resting on the ground.

    Tip of the bucket to the back of the counterweight, with the bucket resting on the ground for transport. This is what has to fit on the trailer and turn around on site.

  • Kubota D1105 dieselEngineThe biggest Kubota in the range. Runs the hydraulics hard all day with a three-pump system.

    Petrol engines are cheaper up front and simpler to look after. Diesels use less fuel per hour, last longer under load and are what most tradies expect. All the Kubota engines here are three-cylinder industrial diesels with parts available Australia-wide. This machine: Kubota D1105 diesel, 3 cylinder, 18.2 kW.

  • 1,800 mmTrack on the groundThe length of track on the ground. Longer tracks mean more stability when the arm is stretched out.

    The length of rubber track touching the ground. Longer tracks spread the weight, which matters on soft lawns and when the arm is stretched out with a full bucket.

Pre-delivery checks

Done on every machine before it leaves the yard.

  • Every fluid checked and topped: engine oil, hydraulic oil, coolant, grease points.
  • Track tension set and all track bolts torqued.
  • Every hose and fitting checked under pressure for leaks.
  • Controls tested through the full range, including the swing boom and thumb.
  • Engine run in and serviced before it leaves the yard.
  • Attachments fitted and checked on the hitch.
  • A walk-through with you at handover, in person or on video.
